subject: Some questions on GMM for 3D data

messages.author: 96a78639336ed702
messages.subject: Some questions on GMM for 3D data
parts:
Hi everyone, I have some experience with GMM for 2D data but I am recently moving forward to 3D data. With such move, I come across some new problems.

1. I am using 3dMD to obtain 3D facial stereo-photogrammetric images of my participants. I noted that the margin of the images are irregular (see image blow)
It can be clearly seem from the image above that the margins of the imaged objects are serrated (indicated by the yellow arrow). More importantly, when I am studying facial shape using GMM, I am not interested in regions such as the neck in the above image. Although regions like the neck are unwanted, semilandmarks will still be automatically placed upon such regions when the samples are digitized in geomorph. I wish to know is there a way to trim off the unwanted regions from 3D data in ply format. Or should I use some other 3D digitization software that allows me to choose where to place semilandmarks?

2. How can I determine the optimal number of curve and surface semilandmarks to place on the region of interest?
Page 3 of the paper "Toward integration of geometric morphometrics and computational biomechanics" stated that "To determine the optimal number of landmarks for performing the warps,a separate sensitivity analysis was conducted using 5 different landmark configurations and densities ranging from using 92 single landmark points to using a combination of 20 single landmarks in addition to 540 pseudolandmarks and slid semilandmarks. Accuracy of warps was judged by warping the V. gouldii mesh to the target shape of the L. borneesis mesh and comparing the bending displacement in the warp with that in the original L. borneesis." However, I still do not know how the "warps" and the "bending displacement" were determined. Can geomorph or any other software help in such determination?

3. After statistical analyses, say regression of shape on centroid size, I obtained procrustes coordinates of the predicted facial shape of the specimens at a particular centroid size. Now I wish to visualize the predicted facial shape, not by separate landmarks as can be obtained from the plotAllSpecimens function in geomorph, but with textures included. I want to know how can I obtain a 3D image of the predicted facial shape with textures included? What software should I use? Amira, Harpoon, Edgewarp (Linux system only?), Viewbox4, IDAV Landmark, or Stratovan Checkpoint?
.
